day_shape: 75 items: IRGC says a tanker struck a mine in the Strait of Hormuz, CENTCOM's Adm. Cooper says the strait remains 'open for business' and accuses Iran-backed militias of funnelling cash to the IRGC, WSJ reports Iran provided Houthi targeting intelligence for Saudi strikes, UK jails Norwegian teen 20 years in Iran-linked murder plot, and Khamenei issues a Nurses' Day/Zaynab message cycle.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz tanker and blockade
threads.summary: The IRGC said a tanker exploded after hitting a mine in the Strait of Hormuz, while CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper said the strait 'remains open for business'. Defa Press commentary framed US naval pressure as a 'maritime blockade' and said Iran retaining control of Hormuz would be a strategic defeat for Washington.

threads.label: Iran–Houthi targeting and Saudi strikes
threads.summary: The Wall Street Journal, cited by Jerusalem Post and Iran International, reported Iran provided Houthi targeting intelligence for strikes on Saudi Arabia, while a Yemeni insider told Iran International Tehran built the Houthi network via Hezbollah and IRGC officers. The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted missiles and drones over Saudi Arabia and the Red Sea, and Defa Press/IRIB claimed Yemeni strikes hit Khamis Mushait, Abha, Marib and an Aramco building in Dhahran.

threads.label: CENTCOM on IRGC financing of militias
threads.summary: CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper said Iran-backed militias including Hezbollah and Hamas are funnelling money back to the IRGC and withholding pay from their own fighters under economic pressure. CENTCOM also issued a video update from the commander the same day.

threads.label: Iran-linked plots in Europe
threads.summary: A Norwegian teenager recruited online by a Swedish organised-crime group that UK prosecutors link to the Iranian government was sentenced in Britain to 20 years for a murder plot. Germany's foreign minister said Berlin will not tolerate Iran's hostile activities, and Jerusalem Post said the absence of a claim for the attempted hijacking of flydubai FZ1073 does not clear Iran.

threads.label: Iran oil and fuel exports under blockade
threads.summary: Reuters, cited by Iran International and Jerusalem Post, reported Iran has exported jet fuel to Myanmar and shipped at least eight LPG cargoes out of the Gulf of Oman since mid-July despite the US naval blockade. Jerusalem Post also reported a now-ousted US general had warned before the war with Iran that American missile-defence munitions stocks were critically low.

threads.label: Khamenei Nurses' Day / Zaynab message cycle
threads.summary: Khamenei's office released the Supreme Leader's message for the birth of Lady Zaynab and Nurses' Day, with multiple excerpts posted on the 'Zaynabi presence' of Iranian women, the role of nurses, and Ashura steadfastness. Defa Press framed the message around an 'incomparable mission' of the Iranian nation in the 'third Sacred Defence'.

threads.label: IDF Lebanon intercepts and Gaza operations
threads.summary: The IDF said it launched interceptors at a 'suspicious aerial target' over southern Lebanon where troops are operating, later confirming two further intercepts at a false target with no sirens triggered. The IDF also announced it killed Hamas Nukhba cell commander Maher Walid Omar al-Husseini in Gaza, and said a female foreign journalist was injured during a confrontation dispersed by forces near Khirbet Abu Falah.

events.summary_en: Fatal fire in Bangladesh; at least 10 dead and 9 injured. A fire in a tourist accommodation on the coast of the Cox Bazar area in south-east Bangladesh left at least 10 dead and 9 injured. Bangladesh's fire service stated in a statement that the incident occurred this morning at a wooden accommodation and restaurant on the Inani beach. According to the service, after two fire brigades arrived at the scene and with the cooperation of local authorities and police, the fire was completely extinguished. According to the statement, the fire may have started from the accommodation's kitchen stove or due to a short electrical circuit; however, the exact cause of the incident has not yet been confirmed.
